# OpenCode

> Capture OpenCode transcripts, file changes, tool calls, and token usage with Entire

The OpenCode integration uses a project-level TypeScript plugin and is in preview.

Follow [Set Up an Agent](/agents/setup) for shared installation, verification, and troubleshooting steps.

## Add OpenCode

```bash theme={null}
entire agent add opencode
opencode
```

Entire writes `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. The plugin captures session and turn events, then uses `opencode export` to materialize the full conversation, file changes, tool calls, and token usage.

OpenCode supports commits before a turn ends. Entire refreshes the exported transcript so a checkpoint created mid-turn includes the agent activity available at that point.

## Limitations

OpenCode does not expose subagent lifecycle events. Entire captures the main session. `entire import` cannot import existing OpenCode sessions.

## Resume

`entire session resume BRANCH` restores the recorded session data when needed and prints:

```bash theme={null}
opencode -s SESSION_ID
```

See the [`session resume` command reference](/cli-reference/session#session-resume) for flags and additional behavior.

Read. Here's the full picture from debugging.

## The plugin itself is loaded and firing

- `opencode2 api get /api/plugin` → `entire { status: active }`
- `entire status` / `entire session list` show OpenCode sessions with captured prompts (e.g. this session's `"read https://docs.entire.io/agents/setup"`)
- `.entire/logs/entire.log` has `agent":"opencode"` `session-start`/`turn-start`/`turn-end`/`compaction`/`session-end` counts (1501 / 1094 / 374 / 182)
- Checkpoints are being written (`git for-each-ref refs/entire/checkpoints` shows fresh refs)

So the V2 port from the other day is doing its job. The failure is one layer deeper.

## Root cause: Entire's OpenCode transcript pipeline targets OpenCode 1

Entire doesn't read OpenCode's transcript from a file. It shells out:

```go
// cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/cli_commands.go
cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "opencode", "export", sessionID)
```

OpenCode 2 moved and reshaped that command:

| | OpenCode 1 | OpenCode 2 (yours, v2.0.2) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Command | `opencode export <id>` | `opencode session export <id>` |
| Message shape | `messages[].info.{role,tokens,cost}` + `parts[]` | `messages[] = {id,time,text,files,agents,type}` |
| Tokens | per message | aggregate under `.info.{tokens,cost}` |

Reproduce:

```sh
opencode export <session>        # prints root help, exit 0 — writes nothing
opencode session export <session> # valid 1.3MB JSON
```

`opencode export` exiting **0** with help text is the nasty part: Entire stages it, `json.Valid()` fails or the parser yields empty messages, and the transcript never installs. Evidence:

- `.entire/tmp/` has **no** `ses_*.json` cache (Entire's source comment: "the turn-end hook writes it")
- `entire session info ses_f7509705…` → `Checkpoints: 0`, no tokens
- OpenCode sessions in `entire session list` show model/prompt but no token counts, unlike Codex

Net effect: lifecycle + prompt capture work; transcript, tokens, tool calls, and file changes do not. That's "the plugin isn't really working."

## Is Entire open source? Yes

- `github.com/entireio/cli` — **MIT**, Go. Relevant paths:
  - `cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/{cli_commands.go,types.go,transcript.go,lifecycle.go,hooks.go,entire_plugin.ts}`
  - `docs/architecture/agent-guide.md` (§603: "transcript is fetched via `opencode export <sessionID>`")
- External agent integrations: `github.com/entireio/external-agents`; plugin index: `entireio/plugin-index`.

## Protocol docs (read)

`/agents/setup`, `/agents/opencode`, `/agents/overview`, `/agents/agent-integration-protocol/overview`:

- 5 hooks and payloads — ours match exactly: `session-start {session_id}`, `turn-start {session_id,prompt,model}`, `turn-end {session_id,model}`, `compaction {session_id}`, `session-end {session_id}`.
- OpenCode is explicitly **Preview**, plugin-based, no subagents, no import.
- Injection is a `{"inject_context":"…"}` envelope read from `turn-start` stdout (our port applies it via the context hook).
- **Detection marker**: Entire identifies its OpenCode file by the string ``Auto-generated by `entire enable --agent opencode` `` (`hooks.go`). Our port dropped that line, which is why `entire agent list` shows `opencode` **unchecked** — Entire thinks it's not installed.

## Two traps to be aware of

1. `/agents/opencode` tells users to run `entire agent add opencode`; that calls `InstallHooks`, which rewrites the file whenever content differs from the template — i.e. it will **overwrite our V2 port with the V1 template**, which OpenCode 2 then rejects. Same risk on `entire enable --force`. The upstream template is still V1 even on `main`.
2. Nothing upstream tracks this yet. I checked the issue list: no `session export` / OpenCode-2 report (closest open ones are #2001 prompt ordering and #1998/older). Latest tag is `v0.10.7-nightly…`; installed is `0.10.5`, and `main` still uses `opencode export`.

## Options

1. **Upstream fix (recommended, durable).** Patch the integration to call `opencode session export` and parse the v2 shape (or use OpenCode 2's HTTP API). I can draft an issue/PR with this exact evidence and the two required changes.
2. **Local stopgap.** An `opencode` PATH shim that rewrites `export` → `session export` and translates v2 JSON back to the v1 `{info,messages[].info/parts}` shape so Entire's parser works. Effective but invasive (shadows the real binary for all callers).
3. **Minimal housekeeping.** Re-add Entire's marker to our port so `entire agent list`/`status` recognize OpenCode, and avoid `entire agent add opencode` unless we also re-apply the port.

Which do you want? I'd do (1) plus (3), and only reach for (2) if you need working checkpoints before an upstream release lands.
Okay, yeah, obviously, I mean, we can't really — we are not really using the official OpenCode entire plugin, right? Like, we are creating our own plugin for version two.

Right, but let me sharpen the boundary, because there are two halves and we only own one.

**The integration is split:**

| Half | What it is | Who owns it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenCode-side plugin | `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` — emits lifecycle events by shelling out to `entire hooks opencode …` | **Ours** — we replaced Entire's generated file (V1, won't load in OC2) with a V2 re-shape |
| Entire-side integration | The `entire` Go binary: `hooks opencode`, session/checkpoint state, and the transcript pipeline (`opencode export`, parsing, condensation) | **Entire's** — the official binary |

So: we are not using Entire's *generated plugin file* (it's V1), but we are still using Entire's *official OpenCode hook contract*, unchanged. Same five hook names, same payloads (`{session_id}`, `{session_id,prompt,model}`, `{session_id,model}`). Our file is a re-shape of their integration, not a new one.

**Why that matters for your question:** the piece that's actually broken — `opencode export` and the v1 JSON parser — lives in Entire's Go binary. The plugin has no channel to influence it; its only jobs are lifecycle events and the `inject_context` envelope. So "we made our own plugin" does *not* give us control over transcript/token/tool capture. That's bounded by the CLI.

**If you want to own the integration end-to-end, there is an official path:** the Agent Integration Protocol. You ship an `entire-agent-<name>` executable on `$PATH`; Entire discovers it and calls *your* commands (lifecycle, export, transcript, tokens). You'd implement `export` yourself with `opencode session export` and parse the v2 shape. Then `entire enable --agent opencode2` uses your integration instead of the broken built-in `opencode` one. Downsides: more surface to build/maintain, and it sits *alongside* the built-in `opencode` entry, so you'd manage that separation.

Three real routes:

1. **Upstream fix** — change Entire's built-in opencode agent: command `opencode export` → `opencode session export`, and parse the v2 message shape. Small, two places, benefits everyone. We'd fork/PR.
2. **External agent integration (`entire-agent-*`)** — we own it fully, within Entire's standard. Heavier.
3. **Local CLI shim** — wrap `opencode` so `export` → `session export` + JSON translation. Quick, invasive, throwaway.

My read: (1) is the smallest model that makes the behavior correct, and it's a genuinely small patch since the parser is isolated in `cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/`. Do you want me to read the protocol's command/data-model pages and scope a proper external-agent implementation, or go after the upstream patch?

So is there a limitation in terms of the SDK or what's preventing us from building our own plugin?

Is there a way to do this without doing anything on the entire side and just doing it fully on the OpenCode side?
Good question — let me ground it: check what the plugin SDK actually exposes, and how hard Entire leans on that `opencode export` call.

content.text: The v2 export is richer than I said — per-message `tokens`, `cost`, `model`, and typed `content` (text/reasoning/tool) — so a faithful translation is possible. Let me check how Entire handles a transcript-prep failure, which decides the cleanest OpenCode-side approach.

Short answer: no SDK blocker, and yes — it can be done entirely on the OpenCode side. The plugin runs unsandboxed in the server process, so it has `node:child_process`, `fs`, and control over the environment it hands to `entire`. The only real constraint is Entire's hook contract (lifecycle JSON only), and that turns out to be workable around.

## Why it's possible

I traced both sides:

**Entire treats a transcript-prep failure as non-fatal.** In `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go`:

```go
if preparer, ok := agent.AsTranscriptPreparer(ag); ok {
    if err := preparer.PrepareTranscript(ctx, transcriptRef); err != nil {
        logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to prepare transcript", ...)   // warn only
    }
}
if !fileExists(transcriptRef) { return fmt.Errorf("transcript file not found: %s", transcriptRef) }
```

So if the cache file exists, it proceeds. And `fetchAndCacheExport` **stages** the `opencode export` output and only renames over the cache if the JSON is valid — on the v2 help-text/empty output it returns early and deletes the staging file. The existing `.entire/tmp/<sessionID>.json` is never clobbered.

**The v2 export is rich enough to translate faithfully.** I checked a real `opencode session export` payload: per-message `tokens`, `cost`, `model`, and typed `content[]` (`text` / `reasoning` / `tool` with `state`). Entire's parser expects exactly `{info, messages:[{info:{role,time,tokens,cost}, parts:[…]}]}` — so a v2→v1 mapping recovers text, reasoning, tool calls (which drive file-change/tool capture), and token usage.

## Two ways to do it — OpenCode side only

**A. Plugin seeds Entire's cache (primary, least invasive).**
On turn boundaries the plugin runs `opencode session export <id>` (the correct v2 command), maps it to Entire's v1 shape, and writes it atomically to `$repo/.entire/tmp/<sessionID>.json`. Entire's own `opencode export` then fails, logs a warning, finds the seeded file, and condenses it. No changes to `entire`, no PATH games.

- Path is deterministic: `sessionTranscriptPath()` → `<worktree>/.entire/tmp/<sessionID>.json`.
- Covers the normal flow: turn-end, commit condensation, `entire checkpoint`/`why`.
- Caveat: refresh timing. Turn-start/turn-end writes cover normal turns; a commit *mid-turn* could see the previous boundary unless we also refresh on a tool/step event.

**B. Plugin injects an `opencode` shim into the `entire` child env.**
The plugin already spawns `entire`; pass `env.PATH = shimDir + ":" + process.env.PATH`. `shimDir/opencode` intercepts `export <id>` → `session export <id>` → v2→v1 → stdout. Then Entire's export genuinely succeeds (no warning).

- Doesn't cover user-invoked Entire (`entire session attach`) or the git-hook invocation, because those don't inherit the plugin's env — for those you'd need the shim on the user's real `PATH` or fall back to A's seeded cache.

Best coverage is **A, optionally plus a globally-installed B** if you want `entire session attach` to work too.

## Caveats (worth deciding on)

- We'd own a v2→v1 adapter against a beta schema; it breaks if OpenCode changes the export shape again.
- This is genuinely "our integration" — it stops being Entire's OpenCode agent and becomes a compatibility shim around Entire's CLI. But it uses only public surfaces (hook contract + `opencode session export`), so it's supportable.
- OpenCode actually exposes the same data via `ctx.session.context()` / the HTTP API, so we could avoid shelling out to `opencode` entirely and build the v1 payload from the SDK. Cleaner, but more mapping work.
- If we go this route, decide whether to keep Entire's marker or intentionally make Entire treat the plugin as unmanaged.

## Two related notes

- `ENTIRE_TEST_OPENCODE_MOCK_EXPORT=1` exists in Entire's code to skip the export and use a pre-written file. Setting it for the child would silence the warning, but it's an integration-test backdoor, not a contract — I'd avoid depending on it.
- None of this fixes `entire agent add opencode` overwriting the plugin. If we own the file, we should keep the marker decision deliberate.

If you want, I'll build **A** as a self-contained module next to the plugin (v2→v1 mapper + cache writer, invoked at turn boundaries), keep the lifecycle hooks as-is, and verify it by running a real turn and checking `entire checkpoint explain` shows transcript/tokens/tools. Want me to scope the mapper first so you can review the field mapping before I wire it in?

Yes — upstream is the right long-term fix. One correction to the framing: "custom plugin + forked CLI" should not be two permanent artifacts. The destination is both fixes upstream, after which your hand-rolled plugin goes away.

## Why upstream is correct

The breakage is entirely in Entire's code, and it affects every OpenCode 2 user:

- **Go side** (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/`): `opencode export` → `opencode session export`, plus the new `{info, messages[]{type,tokens,cost,model,content[]}}` schema.
- **Template side** (`entire_plugin.ts`): still V1, which OC2 rejects, so `entire enable --agent opencode` emits a file that won't load.

A local shim or cache-seeding makes it work *for you*; neither is the right permanent home for a bug that's Entire's to fix, and both are maintenance burden against a beta schema and a very active upstream (8,675 commits, OpenCode owner `Soph` actively merging).

## The correction: the plugin isn't a separate deliverable

If the PR updates `entire_plugin.ts` to the V2 shape, then `entire agent add opencode` regenerates the correct file and your committed `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` becomes unnecessary. Contribute our port *as the template*. Don't maintain a bespoke plugin plus a forked CLI — that doubles the surface for no gain.

## Practical shape of the work

1. **File an issue first** with the evidence (command moved; `opencode export` exits 0 with help; schema diff; no `.entire/tmp/<id>.json` ever written), and ask whether they want a PR. This avoids duplicating whatever their team may already be doing for OC2 GA. Cross-reference open PR #2155 (token counting) so the token mapping aligns.
2. **One coherent PR** off `main`:
   - `cli_commands.go`: prefer `opencode session export <id>`, fall back to `opencode export <id>` for OpenCode 1.
   - `types.go` / `transcript.go` / `transcript/compact/opencode.go`: parse the v2 schema (typed `content`, per-message `tokens`/`cost`/`model`), keep the v1 path. Map unknown part types through tolerantly.
   - `entire_plugin.ts`: dual export (V2 `Plugin.define` default + V1 `server()`) so OC1 users aren't broken — the OpenCode docs explicitly support this.
   - Tests/fixtures: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/*_test.go`, `integration_test/opencode_hooks_test.go`, `e2e/agents/opencode*`, `testdata/opencode_*.jsonl`.
3. **Local build is the bridge, not the destination.** Good news from your setup: the hooks call `entire` via `command -v entire` (no absolute path baked in), so building to `~/.local/bin/entire` and backing up the release binary swaps it cleanly.
   - Build the binary you *run* from the release tag (`v0.10.6`) plus only this fix; PR from `main`. That avoids unrelated `main` churn in your daily driver.
   - `git-remote-entire` only matters if you use `entire://` clone.
4. **Interim while the PR is in review:** use the plugin-side cache seeding, so you're not blocked on the PR. Keep those shims *out* of the PR.

## Caveats to decide

- Entire labels OpenCode **Preview**; they may prefer to own the fix. The issue-first step de-risks that, but accept the possibility they take it in a different direction.
- A V2-only template is a real breaking change for OpenCode 1 users — dual export is the safer contribution.
- If upstream stalls and you need it, options degrade to: keep a rebased fork (fine, bounded), or build an `entire-agent-*` external integration you fully own (heavier, duplicates their built-in).

## My recommendation

Issue → PR (CLI parser + template, one PR, two commits) → local build for now → delete the custom plugin file once a release carries the fix. That leaves no Samva-specific shim in the long run and gives you working capture immediately.

content.text:
Scoped against `~/Developer/entire-cli` (clean `main`, Go 1.27.1, mise ready). Here's the change map. It's bigger than "two lines" — OpenCode 2 moved **two** commands and changed the export schema, and the raw transcript must stay native for resume.

## What's broken (from source + live v2 export)

| Surface | OpenCode 1 (current code) | OpenCode 2 (GA) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Export | `opencode export <id>` | `opencode session export <id>` |
| Import | `opencode import <file>` | `opencode session import <file>` |
| Delete | `opencode session delete` | unchanged |
| Message shape | `messages[].info{role,tokens,cost}` + `parts[]` | `messages[].{type,tokens,cost,model,content[]{text,reasoning,tool}}` |
| Session info | `info{createdAt,updatedAt}` | `info.time{created,updated}` |

`opencode export` on v2 exits **0** printing help, which is why Entire silently caches nothing.

## Change map

**Go — `cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/`**

1. `cli_commands.go`
   - `runOpenCodeExportToFile`: try `opencode session export <id>`, fall back to `opencode export <id>`; keep file redirection and error classification.
   - `runOpenCodeImport`: `opencode session import <file>`, fall back to `opencode import <file>`.
   - `runOpenCodeSessionDelete`: no change.
2. `types.go`: keep internal `ExportSession` (v1) as the canonical **read** model; add v2 input structs + `NormalizeExportSession()` that detects v1/v2 and maps `type→role`, `content[]→parts[]` (text/reasoning/tool), `state`, `tokens`, `cost`, `time`.
3. `transcript.go`: `ParseExportSession` uses the normalizer; everything downstream (prompts, tokens, modified files, position, slicing) is then unchanged.
4. `opencode.go`: `ChunkTranscript`/`ReassembleTranscript` must stop round-tripping through the typed v1 struct (that drops v2 fields and breaks `session import`). Make them **shape-preserving** — split/merge the raw `messages` array while keeping the native JSON — so the stored raw transcript stays importable on both versions.
5. `transcript/compact/opencode.go`: teach the condensed-transcript path the v2 `content[]` shape (separate package, own structs; depends on whether importing `agent/opencode` cycles).
6. Free wins via (3): `strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:1589`, `summarize/summarize.go:276`.

**Plugin template + tests**
7. `entire_plugin.ts`: rewrite to the OpenCode 2 plugin API. Recommend **dual** default export (`Plugin.define({id,setup})` for V2 + `server()` for V1), keeping the `Auto-generated by \`entire enable --agent opencode\`` marker. This is the piece that removes our custom plugin.
8. `hooks_test.go`: assertions currently pin V1 internals (`EntirePlugin`, `experimental.chat.system.transform`, Bun-global checks). Rewrite for the V2 shape + marker.

**Tests/fixtures**
9. `transcript_test.go`: v2 fixture (prompts/tokens/files/position).
10. `cli_commands_test.go`: stub `session export`/`session import` + fallback paths.
11. `transcript/compact/opencode_test.go` + testdata: v2 fixture.
12. `integration_test/opencode_hooks_test.go`: mock env still works; add v2 assertion.
13. `e2e/agents/opencode*.go`: pins `@opencode-ai/plugin` and the running binary version; needs `@opencode/plugin` + OC 2. **Riskiest, least-certain piece.**

**Docs**: `docs/architecture/agent-guide.md` references `opencode export`; update.

## Decisions before I touch the clone

1. **Plugin: dual V1+V2 or V2-only?** Recommend dual (keeps OC1 users; the OpenCode docs support the object+`server()` form, though pre-1.18.29 V1 is fuzzy).
2. **PR shape: one PR or two?** Recommend one PR, two commits (Go capture fix; plugin template + tests). They're both required for OC2 to work end-to-end.
3. **e2e depth:** full OC2 e2e is the unknown. Recommend a minimal, version-gated update and flag it in the PR rather than blocking on it.

## Execution (your sequence)

Fork + branch off `main` → implement + unit/integration tests → `mise run build` (or `go build`) → back up and swap `~/.local/bin/entire` (hooks call `entire` via PATH, no absolute path baked in, so this is clean) → run a real turn and verify `entire checkpoint explain` shows transcript/tokens/tools and the resume path imports → **check in with you** → push branch to fork and open the PR.

Want me to proceed with defaults 1=dual, 2=one PR, 3=minimal e2e? If yes, I'll branch and start with the Go export/import + normalizer (the part that makes capture actually work), then the template, and stop for your check-in after the local build test.

content.text:
Here's the mechanical reality that should decide this:

**OpenCode loads every file in `.opencode/plugins/`, not a version-selected one.** A V1-shaped file makes OpenCode 2 log `PluginModule.LoadError`; a V2 file makes OpenCode 1 log `must default export an object with server()`. So two files sitting side by side each produce a load error in the other runtime. "Separate plugins" can't mean "two files coexist" — it has to mean **one active file, chosen for the installed major**.

Given that, the clean version of what you're describing is:

**Two separate, idiomatic templates in the Go source, selected at install time.**
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/entire_plugin_v1.ts` — today's template, untouched.
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/entire_plugin_v2.ts` — our V2 port, idiomatic V2, no `server()`, no shared-core gymnastics.
- `plugin.go` embeds both; `renderPlugin(ctx)` runs `opencode --version` (`opencode v2.0.2` → major `2`) and returns the matching template.
- `InstallHooks` writes the match; `CheckHookConfig` compares against the match, so upgrading OpenCode 1→2 makes `entire status`/`doctor` flag drift and prompt `entire agent add opencode --force` (or `entire enable`).
- Marker (`Auto-generated by \`entire enable --agent opencode\``) unchanged.

No dual entrypoint, no shared core, each template idiomatic for its API. The extra Go surface is small: a version probe + selection + a test for each.

**The cost, stated plainly:** a committed plugin file is now major-specific. A repo whose teammates run *different* OpenCode majors breaks one group until they reinstall. Dual is the only design that survives that; separate cannot, by construction. For a personal repo that's fine; for a shared OSS repo it's a real tradeoff.

Three decisions:

1. **Does OpenCode 1 support actually matter?** OpenCode 2 is GA and your `opencode` is already 2.0.2. If the answer is "no", we ship a single idiomatic V2 template and delete the version dance entirely — simplest PR, and likely what upstream wants for a Preview integration.
2. **If V1 matters:** version-detected generation from two separate templates (above). Fallback when `opencode` isn't on PATH at install time — I'd leave an existing file alone, else default V2.
3. **Rejected alternative:** separate *agents* (`opencode` vs `opencode2`), each with its own file. Cleanest isolation, but it forks agent identity, hook namespace (`entire hooks opencode*`), and session IDs, and needs a rename when V1 dies. I don't recommend it.

My preference, absent a reason to keep V1: **drop V1, ship the single V2 template.** If you want V1 preserved, do option 2. Which way do you want to go?

### JSON Format (OpenCode pattern)

Single JSON object with `info` and `messages` array. Messages contain `parts` (text, tool calls with state). Similar to Gemini's pattern but with a different schema:

```json
{"info": {"id": "...", "title": "..."}, "messages": [{"info": {"role": "user"}, "parts": [{"type": "text", "text": "..."}]}]}
```

Key difference: OpenCode stores transcripts in a database, not files. The transcript is fetched via `opencode export <sessionID>` at turn-end and cached to `.entire/tmp/<sessionID>.json`.

**Chunking:** Parse JSON, distribute messages across chunks (each chunk is complete JSON with `info` + subset of `messages`).
**Reassembly:** Merge message arrays from all chunks, preserve `info` from first chunk.
**Position:** Message count (`len(session.Messages)`).
**Offset:** Start iterating messages at index N.

### JSONL Format (Pi pattern)

Pi uses JSONL (one JSON object per line) with a tree-shaped entry model. Every entry has `id` and optional `parentId`, enabling Pi's `/fork` and `/clone` branching. Each entry has `type` (`"message"` for conversational entries), `timestamp`, and (for message entries) a `message` object with `role`, `content`, and optional `usage`:

25: ## Title
26: 
27: Use Conventional Commit style unless the repo has a stronger convention:
28: 
29: ```text

31: fix(scope): repair thing
32: refactor(scope): simplify thing
33: docs(scope): update thing

44: ## Body Depth
45: 
46: A small PR can be one outcome sentence and a few bullets. Use only the template sections that help
47: review; a heading is not a requirement to invent content.
48: 
49: - Describe the final aggregate change against the PR's actual base. Omit intermediate commits,
50:   abandoned approaches, review-round history, and commentary about the diff getting smaller.
51: - Lead with the problem and resulting behavior. Use short bullets for supporting detail and code,
52:   diagrams, or examples for mechanics. Link relevant code when it saves the reviewer a search.
53: - Omit routine “ran tests” or “CI passed” boilerplate from the body. Keep validation evidence in the
54:   delivery report and checks. Include a reproduction, benchmark method, unusual manual check,
55:   coverage limitation, or failure when it changes how the reviewer should assess the patch. Always
56:   retain required repository-template fields and disclose material validation gaps.

58:   context, design rationale, code examples, and before/after evidence. Concision is not a length
59:   cap.

62: evidence. Keep each useful aid unless it is stale, invalid, redundant, or replaced by something
63: clearer. Do not silently reduce screenshot or artifact coverage while polishing prose.

67: ## Code-First Body

69: Select the smallest artifact set that makes the change reviewable:
70: 
71: - **Public API or developer experience:** show a copyable usage example first.
72: - **Simple linear flow:** show a compact ASCII diagram.
73: - **Multi-actor protocol, request sequence, or state transitions:** show a Mermaid sequence or state
74:   diagram.
75: - **Algorithm, reconciliation, or ownership rule:** show the decisive implementation snippet or
76:   pseudocode.
77: - **Behavioral change:** show a focused before/after example or input/output table.
78: - **Configuration or schema:** show the changed shape with representative values.
79: - **User-visible UI:** show screenshots under `Screenshots`.
80: 
81: Use real names and signatures from the diff. Trim setup, imports, boilerplate, and unrelated error
82: handling; snippets should normally fit on one screen. A code block must reveal usage or behavior,
83: not reproduce the diff for decoration.
84: 
85: Use one focused visual artifact when it answers the reviewer's question faster than prose. A file
86: tree explains ownership, a call tree explains runtime control flow, Mermaid explains several actors
87: or state transitions, and a before/after or input/output view explains behavior. For UI-heavy work,
88: add one focused HTML artifact only when screenshots and static diagrams cannot show the interaction
89: or layout clearly. Keep it tied to the PR's final state and make it easy to open or inspect.

96:   <SessionToolbar>

183: information shape:

185: | Draft contains                                                       | Replace with                                                 |
186: | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |

189: | Several actors exchanging requests, keys, events, or retries         | Mermaid `sequenceDiagram`                                    |

215: 
216: One or two sentences explaining the reviewer-relevant outcome.

221: - Concrete change two.

233:

235: 
236: Select and publish media with [pr-media](pr-media.md). Keep media as local files until upload, then
237: read back the body and confirm its GitHub attachments render. An artifact gallery is supplementary;
238: a gallery-only Screenshots section does not satisfy PR readiness. This applies to standalone and
239: stacked PRs.

243: loading, empty, error, or populated states. Capture representative user-facing states after

266: For performance claims, compare a baseline from the target branch with the candidate. Record the
267: exact revisions, workload, environment, units, and relevant sampling or warmup conditions. Use the
268: same method on both. If only one side was measured, report the limit without claiming an
269: improvement.

273: | ----------------- | -------------- | ----------------- | -------------- |
274: | p95 latency (ms)  | measured value | measured value    | measured delta |

289: behavior, storage/query semantics, or scope boundaries.

311: caller
312:   -> public API
313:   -> runtime boundary
314:   -> external system
315:   -> result
316: ```

322:   participant A as Caller
323:   participant B as Runtime
324:   participant C as External system
325:   A->>B: invoke(input)
326:   B->>C: request
327:   C-->>B: result
328:   B-->>A: response
329: ```

332: 
333: Show the decisive reconciliation, state-transition, or ownership code when it explains behavior
334: better than prose:

366: human-owned bullets beside the relevant example or under `Review notes`. Omit bot score history.

384:

## Summary

OpenCode 2 is GA and incompatible with Entire's OpenCode integration in two places, so no transcript was ever captured: the generated plugin uses the OpenCode 1 server-hook export (rejected with `PluginModule.LoadError`), and the CLI runs `opencode export`, which OpenCode 2 answers with a help page and exit 0.

## Changes

- **Plugin** — emit an OpenCode 2 plugin definition (`id` + `setup`): session hooks replace `experimental.chat.system.transform`, the event subscription replaces the event map, and `session-end` moves to plugin unload. The SDK import is type-only so the loader does not resolve project `node_modules`. Drops OpenCode 1 plugin support.
- **Commands** — try `opencode session export` / `session import` (OpenCode 2) and validate the output before accepting it, falling back to `opencode export` / `import` (OpenCode 1). The v1 command exits 0 with a help page on OpenCode 2, so the exit code alone cannot be trusted.
- **Schema** — normalize both export shapes (`info`/`parts` vs `type`/`content` plus a message-level `text`) to the v1 model for reads, and keep chunking/reassembly byte-preserving so the stored raw transcript stays importable by `opencode session import`.

## Flow

```text
turn-end hook
  -> opencode session export <id>   (fallback: opencode export <id>)
  -> validate JSON (rejects exit-0 help output)
  -> .entire/tmp/<id>.json          (native, importable)
  -> ParseExportSession             (normalized v1 view for prompts/tokens/files)
```

## Review notes

- The exit-0-help behavior is why the command result is validated rather than trusted.
- OpenCode 1 plugin support is intentionally dropped; the CLI keeps the v1 export/import fallback.

## Keeping the dev build

Installed at `~/.local/bin/entire`, currently `0.0.0-20260912160713-d6d864f76c4f` (HEAD of the PR branch). Backup remains `~/.local/bin/entire.bak-0.10.5`.

One operational gotcha worth knowing: the earlier `exit 137` noise was **not** the update check — it was macOS killing processes when I `cp`'d over a running binary in place. Replace it by unlinking first:

```sh
cd ~/Developer/entire-cli && go build -o /tmp/entire-local ./cmd/entire/
rm -f ~/.local/bin/entire && cp /tmp/entire-local ~/.local/bin/entire
```

## Auto-update: config-based disable

Short answer: **no, not today.** In `cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/` the only disable is the env kill switch `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` (`autoupdate.go:18`); `CheckAndNotify` consults nothing else.

But you likely don't need it:
- `CheckAndNotify` returns early for dev builds — `isDevBuild` treats a Go pseudo-version (`0.0.0-<ts>-<hash>`) as unreleased (`versioncheck.go:29`). Your build matches that form, so it never prompts.
- For a **released** build (brew/mise/install.sh), a "Skip until next version" choice persists in `~/.config/entire/version_check.json` (`SkippedVersion`), but that's per-release, not a permanent disable. There is no `auto_update: false` setting and `entire configure` doesn't expose one.

If you want a durable config switch, I can add one upstream — the natural shape is a global setting in `~/.config/entire/settings.json` (or a `disabled` flag in `version_check.json`) honored by `CheckAndNotify`, plus an `entire configure` flag.
